# There Is Absolutely Nothing New in the Pragmatic Method[^1]

There is absolutely nothing new in the pragmatic method, a method of settling metaphysical disputes that otherwise might be interminable. Socrates was an adept at it. Aristotle used it methodically. Locke, Berkeley and Hume made momentous contributions to truth by its means. Shadworth Hodgson keeps insisting that realities are only what they are 'known-as.' But these forerunners of pragmatism used it in fragments: they were preluders only. Not until in our time has it generalized itself, become conscious of a universal mission, pretended to a conquering destiny.

[^1]: [[@Pragmatism - William James]]
